evidence:
+cat.balance = pp.Balance{logic_hz = wire_test_logic_hz, max_ticks = 100000, snap_radius = 36, map_w_tiles = 40, map_h_tiles = 30, tile_px = 26, packet_bandwidth = 120}

evidence:
-testing.expectf(t, res_drops == 0,
+testing.expectf(t, res_drops < uplink_drops,
+// in one tick) make ONE thin (40 u/s) sink shed once across the whole run

title: W9 comment claims clamp-honest landable (14600) above raw accrual (12900) — impossible per its own formula
evidence:
+// host 333 → every 4 ticks = 0.25/tick). The landable is the
+// clamp-honest sum (measured 14600 vs the raw-accrual 12900 —
+// the clamp formula is the exact bound).
+eff := WINDOW / ((1000 + acc - 1) / acc)
detail: Per terminal, WINDOW/ceil(1000/acc) <= WINDOW*acc/1000, so the clamped sum cannot exceed the raw sum over the same roster. The quoted comparison is unit-incoherent or wrong.
recommended_fix: Recompute or restate the parenthetical so the comparison is meaningful.

+// 333 milli/tick → one pick every ~3 ticks), so the boundaries pin the

title: PR body's 'same 3.2x headroom' claim is false by its own table

+| typical route, estate_surge demo (measured `--stats-out`): email | 172 ms | **555 ms** | 3.2× |

title: Surge window-boundary pins degraded from ==1 to <=1
evidence:
-testing.expectf(t, tick_class_count(&state.flow, 399, 1) == 1, "surge must NOT be active at tick 399, got %d", tick_class_count(&state.flow, 399, 1))
+testing.expectf(t, tick_class_count(&state.flow, 399, 1) <= 1, "surge must NOT amplify at tick 399, got %d", tick_class_count(&state.flow, 399, 1))
-testing.expectf(t, tick_class_count(&state.flow, 600, 1) == 1, "surge must end at tick 600, got %d", tick_class_count(&state.flow, 600, 1))
+testing.expectf(t, tick_class_count(&state.flow, 600, 1) <= 1, "surge must end at tick 600, got %d", tick_class_count(&state.flow, 600, 1))
detail: <=1 holds whether the window is active or not (0 or 1 pick either way); the set-piece boundary semantics at ticks 399/600 are no longer distinguished.
recommended_fix: Pin exact credit-phase ticks at the window edges, or assert a measurable in-window vs out-of-window difference.
